## Authentication
Authorization Header — Authentication method detected from captured traffic.

### Providing credentials
- Prefer passing auth as request headers or cookies at call time (do not hardcode secrets into the skill).
- If executing via an external proxy/executor, pass per-call credentials (cookies and/or headers) so they are not persisted.

## Dependencies
- Runtime capable of HTTPS requests.
- If using `scripts/api.ts`: TypeScript toolchain (or transpile to JS).

## Endpoints

### Auth Flow (2)
- `GET /personalize/client_data/{client_dataToken}` — Obtain client data using a token.
- `GET /personalize/user_data/{user_dataToken}` — Obtain user data using a token.

### Data Read (3)
- `GET /_i18n/_lhzcyzq/en-us/messages.json` — Download localization messages.
- `GET /data` — Retrieve general data.
- `GET /pagead/conversion/{timestamp}` — Get conversion data for a timestamp.

### Data Write (4)
- `POST /{id}` — Create or update a resource by ID.
- `POST /com.snowplowanalytics.snowplow/tp2` — Send tracking data to Snowplow.
- `POST /v2/{v2Id}` — Create or update a resource using v2 ID.
- `POST /w/{wId}/{1Id}/visitor_events` — Send visitor events.

### Core API (2)
- `POST /api/{apiId}/envelope` — Send an envelope to a GitLab API.
- `POST /w/{wId}/{1Id}/sentry/proxy` — Proxy Sentry events.

## About This Skill

This skill provides access to Gitlab's internal API — the hidden endpoints that power their web/mobile app.
These are NOT official public APIs. They were captured by observing network traffic while using the site.

**Important:**
- Auth tokens in `auth.json` may expire — re-capture if you get 401 errors
- Internal APIs can change without notice — endpoints may break
- Rate limits are unknown — be conservative with request frequency

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when you need to:
- Access Gitlab data without official API access
- Automate actions on gitlab.com (faster than browser automation)
- Call the same endpoints the Gitlab frontend uses
